name: application-sports-scoreboard
title: Sports Scoreboard
description: Two-team scoreboard with period/clock and a possession indicator, where the leading team is derived by comparing real scores — distinct from a generic stats display, which has no live clock or possession semantics.
useWhen: Showing a live or in-progress game's score alongside period and clock.
You want the leading team visually distinguished, computed from the real scores.
Possession matters (basketball, football) and should be marked on the possessing team.
avoidWhen: You need a generic post-game stats summary with no live clock — use a stats table instead.
The sport has no possession concept (e.g. baseball, tennis) — omit the possession icon.
You need a play-by-play event timeline — use live-match-timeline instead.
responsiveBehavior: The two team columns share equal width via flex-1 and remain side-by-side at any supported width; the period/clock row stays centered below.
accessibility: The possession icon carries an aria-label of 'Has possession' rather than relying on icon shape alone.
The leading team's score and abbreviation use higher-contrast text than the trailing team's, not color hue alone.
Score and clock values use tabular-nums so digit widths don't shift as they update.

variants.title: Sports scoreboard
variants.description: A 78–82 fourth-quarter game with the home team leading and holding possession, on a light surface.
accessibility: The leading team is computed by comparing the two real score values, never hand-picked independently of the scores shown.

variants.title: Sports scoreboard (Dark)
variants.description: The same 78–82 game, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Leading vs trailing team text colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
